I'm also flagging serious compliance gaps alongside this: a shared 'admin' credential used from the bastion with no per-person attribution, IAM auth disabled, missing audit log export, out-of-band manual changes bypassing change management on an IaC-managed cluster, deletion protection off, and only one day of backup retention -- all of which add real SLA breach risk on top of the outage itself.

", "signature": "", "type": "thinking"}, {"text": "The connections-high alarm fired because about 90 idle sessions are open on the writer, and 90 is its connection ceiling. The parameter-group change made at the same moment did not cause it. If the cluster's tags are accurate, checkout is at risk of failing to connect to its database. That's worth up to $5,100/min, the SLA (service level agreement) would be breached around 23:38–23:40 UTC, and the data is tagged Confidential.

## Technical cause
- **What fired:** `example-connections-high` went into alarm at 23:21:46 UTC. `example-cluster-writer` was at 90 connections at 23:20 against a threshold of 70; normally it sits at 0.
- **The sessions are idle:**
  - Connection attempts jumped by about 85–90 over the normal ~27 per 5 minutes.
  - CPU stayed at ~8%, free memory at ~1.0 GB, and read/write throughput (0.5 writes/s, 3.2 reads/s) didn't move.
  - The reader instance has 0 connections.
- **Where they come from:** all 190 disconnect entries in today's error log are user `admin` (the master user) from host `10.0.0.219`, database `appdb`. That IP is the bastion EC2 instance `i-1234567890abcdef0_1` (`example-stack/Bastion`). Earlier batches only went away when the server closed them as idle (19:31:26 and 22:14:46–59).
- **Why it matters:** db.t4g.medium has a default limit of 90 connections, so the writer has no room left. New connections from apps, scale-outs or pool refills would be refused with "Too many connections" (ERROR 1040).
- **It's happened four times today:** about 17:30–18:00, 18:30–20:50, 21:45–22:15, and 23:18 to now (UTC).

## The recent change: it lines up in time, but it can't explain this
- **What changed:** IAM user `example-session` repeatedly created the cluster parameter group `example-cluster-params`, which sets `aurora_fwd_writer_idle_timeout=30`. Each time they attached it to the cluster, then switched back to the default group and deleted it. The latest cycle ran 23:17:17–23:17:21, and each earlier storm also started within minutes of an attach.
- **Why it isn't the cause:**
  - That setting only applies to writes forwarded from reader instances, and the reader has no connections. If anything, it would close idle sessions sooner, not open new ones.
  - Both instances show the new group as `pending-reboot`, so it isn't active yet.
  - A database setting can't make the bastion open 90 logins as `admin`.
- **Most likely link:** whoever ran this test changes the parameter group and runs the connection load from the bastion at the same time. This is unconfirmed.
- **Not yet known:** which process on the bastion opens the sessions. I found no SSM sessions or commands from a person; the only SSM command was routine patching at 21:50, after this batch started. That needs process-level checks on the bastion itself.

## Business impact
All figures come from the cluster's tags; I didn't confirm them.
- **Who is affected:** dependent services are `checkout-service` (CRITICAL), `order-history-api` (HIGH) and `analytics-etl` (MEDIUM). The owning team is Data Platform / DBRE.
- **What it costs:**
  - Revenue is tagged at $5,100/min. About 20 minutes of a checkout outage would be roughly $102K.
  - Today's ~205 minutes at the limit put the theoretical worst case at about $1.05M.
  - The steady existing workload kept its throughput, so actual losses are probably well below that. I can't confirm this without application-side error logs, which I didn't have access to.
- **SLA:** the tagged threshold is 20 minutes. This batch started at about 23:18, so it breaches around 23:38–23:40 UTC unless it's cleared. Earlier batches today (about 30, 140 and 30 minutes) would already have breached it.
- **Compliance exposure (data tagged `Confidential`):**
  - The shared master credential `admin` is being used from a bastion, so there is no per-person accountability.
  - IAM database authentication is off.
  - No audit log is sent to CloudWatch, only error and slow-query logs, so there is little record of what those sessions read.
  - A person changed a CloudFormation-managed cluster directly and repeatedly, which is a change-management gap and drift from the stack.
  - Deletion protection is off and backups are kept for only 1 day.

## Suggested next steps
- **Free up connections now:** stop whatever on the bastion is opening sessions as `admin`, or kill the idle `admin@10.0.0.219` sessions.
- **Prevent a repeat:** give apps their own database users with per-user connection limits, and lower `wait_timeout` from 28800 seconds (8 hours). Consider RDS Proxy or a larger instance class to get more connection headroom.
- **Parameter group:** reverting `example-cluster-params` only cleans up drift. Don't reboot to apply it.

I've started a separate mitigation proposal with these findings, and its report will arrive on its own.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

{"type": "finding", "id": "cause-idle-admin-sessions-exhaust-ceiling", "title": "~90 idle admin sessions from the Bastion fill the writer's 90-connection limit", "description": "In every storm, about 85\u201390 extra connection attempts come from user `admin` (the master user) at 10.0.0.219 (Bastion EC2 i-1234567890abcdef0_1), database `appdb`. The sessions stay idle: CPU, memory and throughput don't change. db.t4g.medium has a default max_connections of 90, so these sessions leave no room. Any new application connection would be refused with ERROR 1040 'Too many connections'. Earlier batches only cleared when the server closed them as idle (19:31:26 and 22:14:46\u201359 UTC). This has happened four times today: ~17:30\u201318:00, 18:30\u201320:50, 21:45\u201322:15, and 23:18 to now. check the count before the kill step.\n\n*Free connection slots by ending only leftover idle admin@10.0.0.219 sessions*\n\n```bash\n# Run on the Bastion via SSM (MYSQL_PWD exported as above)\nH=example-cluster-writer.abcdefghijkl.us-west-2.rds.amazonaws.com\nmysql -h $H -u admin -N -e \"SELECT CONCAT('CALL mysql.rds_kill(',id,');') FROM information_schema.processlist WHERE user='admin' AND host LIKE '10.0.0.219:%' AND db='appdb' AND command='Sleep' AND time>60 AND id<>CONNECTION_ID();\" > /tmp/kill.sql\nwc -l /tmp/kill.sql\nmysql -h $H -u admin < /tmp/kill.sql\n```\n\n**Risks:**\n- Killed sessions can't be restored; Keep bastion or tooling sessions from taking all of the writer's connection slots**\n\nCreate a dedicated least-privilege DB user for bastion tooling with MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS 10, stop tools from using master user admin, manage its credentials in Secrets Manager, and define it in example-stack or its bootstrap scripts.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- No automated process on the bastion connects as admin\n- A runaway bastion client can hold at most 10 connections, leaving at least 80 for application users\n\n**2. Close abandoned idle sessions sooner, and make the limit explicit in infrastructure code**\n\nAttach a custom DB instance parameter group (copied from default.aurora-mysql8.0) in the CloudFormation stack with wait_timeout and interactive_timeout around 300-600 s and an explicit max_connections; roll out in a maintenance window (needs a reboot). Re-evaluate whether db.t4g.medium's 90 connections is enough for checkout-service, order-history-api and analytics-etl.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- Idle sessions are closed within the configured timeout instead of building up for hours\n- The parameter group and instance class are defined in example-stack with no drift\n\n**3. Warn early, before applications start failing**\n\nKeep example-connections-high and add an alarm on the writer's AbortedClients/ConnectionAttempts trend, notifying Data Platform / DBRE.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- The alarm fires before DatabaseConnections reaches 90\n- The alarm notifies the on-call team","children":[]}]}]}]}}

**1. Keep bastion or tooling sessions from taking all of the writer's connection slots**

Create a dedicated least-privilege DB user for bastion tooling with MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS 10, stop tools from using master user admin, manage its credentials in Secrets Manager, and define it in example-stack or its bootstrap scripts.

Acceptance criteria:
- No automated process on the bastion connects as admin
- A runaway bastion client can hold at most 10 connections, leaving at least 80 for application users

**2. Close abandoned idle sessions sooner, and make the limit explicit in infrastructure code**

Attach a custom DB instance parameter group (copied from default.aurora-mysql8.0) in the CloudFormation stack with wait_timeout and interactive_timeout around 300-600 s and an explicit max_connections; roll out in a maintenance window (needs a reboot). Re-evaluate whether db.t4g.medium's 90 connections is enough for checkout-service, order-history-api and analytics-etl.

Acceptance criteria:
- Idle sessions are closed within the configured timeout instead of building up for hours
- The parameter group and instance class are defined in example-stack with no drift

**3. Warn early, before applications start failing**

Keep example-connections-high and add an alarm on the writer's AbortedClients/ConnectionAttempts trend, notifying Data Platform / DBRE.

Acceptance criteria:
- The alarm fires before DatabaseConnections reaches 90

**1. Keep bastion or tooling sessions from taking all of the writer's connection slots**

Create a dedicated least-privilege DB user for bastion tooling with MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS 10, stop tools from using master user admin, manage its credentials in Secrets Manager, and define it in example-stack or its bootstrap scripts.

Acceptance criteria:
- No automated process on the bastion connects as admin
- A runaway bastion client can hold at most 10 connections, leaving at least 80 for application users

**2. Close abandoned idle sessions sooner, and make the limit explicit in infrastructure code**

Attach a custom DB instance parameter group (copied from default.aurora-mysql8.0) in the CloudFormation stack with wait_timeout and interactive_timeout around 300-600 s and an explicit max_connections; roll out in a maintenance window (needs a reboot). Re-evaluate whether db.t4g.medium's 90 connections is enough for checkout-service, order-history-api and analytics-etl.

Acceptance criteria:
- Idle sessions are closed within the configured timeout instead of building up for hours
- The parameter group and instance class are defined in example-stack with no drift

**3. Warn early, before applications start failing**

Keep example-connections-high and add an alarm on the writer's AbortedClients/ConnectionAttempts trend, notifying Data Platform / DBRE.

Acceptance criteria:
- The alarm fires before DatabaseConnections reaches 90

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### Aurora writer connections above threshold
**Description:** example-connections-high went into ALARM at 23:21:46 UTC: example-cluster-writer reached 90 connections at 23:20 against a threshold of 70 (normally 0). 90 is the instance's connection limit, so checkout-service (CRITICAL), order-history-api and analytics-etl are at risk of being refused. The 20-minute SLA tag would be breached around 23:38–23:40 UTC.
**Time:** 2026-11-13T21:45:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: ~90 idle admin sessions from the Bastion fill the writer's 90-connection limit
**Description:** In every storm, about 85–90 extra connection attempts come from user `admin` (the master user) at 10.0.0.219 (Bastion EC2 i-1234567890abcdef0_1), database `appdb`. # Mitigation Summary

## Action
Stop the Bastion process that keeps opening idle admin sessions to appdb, kill leftover idle admin@10.0.0.219 sessions with mysql.rds_kill, then confirm connections stay low for 15+ min. Moving the writer role to a larger class is a fallback only.

## Reasoning
All 90 connection slots on example-cluster-writer (db.t4g.medium, max_connections 90) are held by idle sessions from master user admin on the Bastion i-1234567890abcdef0_1 (10.0.0.219), so checkout-service and order-history-api would get ERROR 1040. Waiting for timeouts has failed four times today, so the source must be stopped. Scaling up only buys time and needs a failover. Reverting example-cluster-params is separate cleanup (no reboot). Checked against safe-deployment policies with no violations; not executed.

ps -eo pid,ppid,user,lstart,etime,cmd --sort=start_time | grep -Ei 'mysql|python|node|java|sysbench|mysqlslap|bash|sh -c' | grep -v grep

sudo systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager

**Purpose:** Free connection slots by ending only leftover idle admin@10.0.0.219 sessions
**Risks:** Killed sessions can't be restored; clients still using them must reconnect.
**Advisory:** The filter excludes active sessions and other hosts, so app connections aren't touched.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Keep bastion or tooling sessions from taking all of the writer's connection slots
**Description:** Create a dedicated least-privilege DB user for bastion tooling with MAX_USER_CONNECTIONS 10, stop tools from using master user admin, manage its credentials in Secrets Manager, and define it in example-stack or its bootstrap scripts.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- No automated process on the bastion connects as admin
- A runaway bastion client can hold at most 10 connections, leaving at least 80 for application users

#### 2. Close abandoned idle sessions sooner, and make the limit explicit in infrastructure code
**Description:** Attach a custom DB instance parameter group (copied from default.aurora-mysql8.0) in the CloudFormation stack with wait_timeout and interactive_timeout around 300-600 s and an explicit max_connections; roll out in a maintenance window (needs a reboot). Re-evaluate whether db.t4g.medium's 90 connections is enough for checkout-service, order-history-api and analytics-etl.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Idle sessions are closed within the configured timeout instead of building up for hours
- The parameter group and instance class are defined in example-stack with no drift

#### 3. Warn early, before applications start failing
**Description:** Keep example-connections-high and add an alarm on the writer's AbortedClients/ConnectionAttempts trend, notifying Data Platform / DBRE.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The alarm fires before DatabaseConnections reaches 90
- The alarm notifies the on-call team
